title: Lakehouse Zero Copy: Iceberg Federation vs Bulk JDBC Copy

steps.prompt: A company keeps 100TB of telemetry in Databricks as Apache Iceberg tables (Parquet). Product wants Data 360 insights on that telemetry without paying to duplicate the lake into Salesforce storage. Which approach is Well-Architected?

options.label: Zero Copy federation via Iceberg REST Catalog metadata, querying Databricks Parquet tables in place
options.rationale: File-based Zero Copy queries Parquet/Iceberg data in place using open catalog metadata, avoiding storage duplication and compute double-billing.

options.label: Scheduled JDBC pipeline extracting 100TB into native Data 360 Data Lake Objects for local processing
options.distractorAntipattern: Extracting lakehouse data into Data 360 duplicates storage costs and introduces heavy batch ingestion latency.
options.rationale: Ingesting 100TB via JDBC duplicates storage, incurs massive credit consumption, and creates substantial data synchronization lag.

options.label: Micro-batch Ingestion API jobs streaming partitioned Parquet chunks into custom CRM staging tables
options.distractorAntipattern: Streaming big data telemetry into core CRM objects violates platform storage limits and triggers API throttling.
options.rationale: The Ingestion API is meant for lightweight JSON/CSV records, not multi-terabyte Parquet dumps, and staging in CRM objects exhausts database quotas.
